results.title: Joby Aviation acquires defense tech startup Resonant Sciences for $500 million as it expands beyond air taxis - Tech Startups
results.content:
The electric air taxi maker said Tuesday it has agreed to acquire Ohio-based defense technology startup Resonant Sciences for roughly $500 million, giving Joby a dedicated defense business at a time when military spending and demand for autonomous aircraft are rising.

Joby expects to pay about $450 million in cash and $50 million in common stock. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027.

Resonant Sciences designs, manufactures, and delivers advanced radio-frequency and mission systems for U.S. national security customers. Once the acquisition closes, Resonant will become Joby’s dedicated defense business, bringing together its existing operations with Joby’s hybrid aircraft and autonomy technologies. [...] The deal marks a significant shift for a company best known for developing electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft, or eVTOLs, for commercial passenger transportation.

Joby’s commercial aircraft business will remain focused on electric air taxis, but the Resonant acquisition gives the company another route into a defense market that has become increasingly attractive to aviation startups.

Military interest in autonomous aircraft, drones, hybrid propulsion, and advanced communications systems has grown amid the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East. For eVTOL companies, defense contracts can offer something the commercial air taxi market has yet to provide at scale: customers willing to pay for aircraft and related technology before mass passenger service becomes commonplace. [...] Investors initially reacted negatively to the deal. Joby shares fell 6.5% in premarket trading Tuesday, Reuters reported.

## From seven-minute air taxi rides to defense technology

The acquisition comes just four months after Joby launched its first electric air taxi flights in New York City, where the company demonstrated trips to John F. Kennedy International Airport in about seven minutes.

That commercial vision remains intact. The Resonant deal shows Joby wants a second business running alongside it.

The combination will give Joby roughly 1 million square feet of manufacturing, integration, and testing space across the Dayton, Ohio region. That footprint could prove valuable as the company moves from aircraft development into larger-scale manufacturing and defense programs.

# Joby Aviation acquires Beavercreek’s Resonant Sciences in $500M deal

Thomas Gnau, Dayton Daily News, Ohio

5 min read

Joby Aviation, the California company that plans to make electric flying taxis in Vandalia and Dayton, is acquiring a Beavercreek defense contractor, Resonant Sciences, in a deal valued at approximately $500 million.

The acquisition will represent a significant expansion of Joby's defense business. The investment also strengthens ties between Joby and the Dayton area. Resonant Sciences has about 250 Dayton-area employees, most of them in Beavercreek.

"This gives us more than a million square feet in Dayton," Joby founder and Chief Executive JoeBen Bevirt told the Dayton Daily News in an exclusive interview. [...] "Demand for advanced defense technology is growing rapidly, and Resonant has built the technology, customer relationships and manufacturing capabilities required to meet it," North said in Joby's statement on the acquisition. "Joining Joby gives our team access to additional engineering depth, aircraft platforms, autonomy technology and production expertise, allowing us to move faster for our existing customers and pursue opportunities that neither company could address alone."

He added: "Resonant's name, leadership, people and commitments to our customers will remain in place. What changes is the scale of what we can build and deliver." [...] "The partnership between Joby Aviation and Resonant Sciences proves something we've long believed about Ohio: when you put companies within a network of innovation, they don't just coexist — they collaborate," said J.P. Nauseef, president and CEO of JobsOhio. "Joby brings world-class strength in designing and scaling advanced electric and hybrid aircraft. Resonant Sciences brings deep expertise in national defense and mission-critical systems. Together, they're tackling some of the most ambitious challenges in aerospace and national security — and they're doing it here."

Last week, Joby said it had signed a lease for 45,000 square feet at Alliance Air Trade Center at Perot Field Fort Worth Alliance Airport in Texas.
